title: Islamic Beliefs: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the foundational Islamic beliefs: Tawhid, the Six Articles of Faith and the nature of Allah.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Islamic Beliefs foundations — Tawhid, Six Articles of Faith, Allah's nature.
final_note: You now know the core beliefs of Sunni Islam and the Shi'a foundations of faith.

concepts.def: The oneness and unity of Allah
Associating partners with Allah — the gravest sin
The afterlife and Day of Judgement
Angels — beings created from light who serve Allah
Predestination — Allah's knowledge of all things

walkthroughs.body_html:
Tawhid — the oneness of Allah — is the central belief of Islam.

Surah 112 (al-Ikhlas): 'He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born. Nor is there to Him any equivalent.'

The opposite is shirk — associating anything with Allah — the gravest sin in Islam.

Sunni Muslims hold Six Articles of Faith:

1. Tawhid (oneness of Allah)
2. Malaikah (angels)
3. Kutub (holy books)
4. Risalah (prophets)
5. Akhirah (afterlife / Day of Judgement)
6. Al-Qadr (predestination)

Shi'a Muslims hold Five Roots of Religion (Usul ad-Din):

1. Tawhid
2. Adalat (justice of Allah)
3. Nubuwwah (prophethood)
4. Imamah (leadership through Imams)
5. Mi'ad (Day of Resurrection)

Both branches agree on Tawhid as the heart of Islam.
